problem: Padding is listed as something the options field can 'add', next to timestamp and route. Padding is not an option type; it is filler bytes (end-of-list / no-op) that make the header a whole number of 32-bit words.
fix: Options, rare today, can carry a timestamp, record route or source route; padding bytes fill the header up to a 32-bit boundary.

problem: The sentence 'so routers and hosts may rate-limit ICMP and fragment queues' joins two unrelated defences. Limiting ICMP does not protect the memory used to hold half-complete fragment sets, so the reason-and-remedy link is broken and students may copy it as cause and effect.
fix: Reassembly at the destination uses memory; too many half-complete fragment sets can exhaust it, so hosts limit the memory or number of sets they hold and discard old ones on timeout. Separately, routers may rate-limit ICMP messages to protect themselves.

problem: 'The offsets jump by 185 and 370' can be read as steps of 185 and then 370, but the offsets are 0, 185 and 370 (each step is 185). The wording is ambiguous about what the numbers are.
fix: The fragment offsets are 0, 185 and 370 because they count 8-byte units (0, 1480 ÷ 8 and 2960 ÷ 8), and the last fragment clears MF.
